stories.title: Venezuela quakes kill 1,400 amid race to find survivors
stories.summary: Rescue crews are racing to find survivors in the rubble of Venezuela's powerful earthquakes as the death toll reached 1,430 and hopes dwindled more than three days after the disaster. Tens of thousands of people were reported missing as collapsed buildings dotted cities in a country already enduring an economic crisis and political upheaval after US special forces captured authoritarian leader Nicolas Maduro in January. Millions of people were also feared to lack sanitation and other basic needs. Experts say the first 72 hours after natural disasters are the key, narrow window for finding the living. After that the search becomes one of recovering bodies.

stories.title: Iran, US continue escalating attacks after tanker struck
stories.summary: Iran and the US continued their attacks in the Gulf as each accused the other of violating an interim deal signed less than two weeks ago to end their four-month-old war. Shortly after President Donald Trump warned the US might "militarily complete the job", Iran early this morning launched missiles and drones on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain, continuing a series of escalating attacks. Beyond the Gulf, Israel said it had struck Iran-backed Hezbollah militants in southern Lebanon as fighting continued in an area Tehran says is key to its peace deal with Washington The US military said earlier it had struck Iran again, hours after a tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most important energy shipping route, which Iran had largely cut off for most of the conflict.

stories.title: The policies that will define Ireland's EU presidency
stories.summary: Ireland's presidency comes at a time of severe challenge for the EU, and that will be reflected in the intensity of the legislative programme the Government will have to steer through. The EU has been consumed by war in Ukraine and the Middle East and the high energy prices that followed. It is undergoing a painful divorce from the Trump Administration, one which involves a dramatic recalibration of its security and defence policies. There are big challenges in Europe’s relationship with China, whether through accusations of Chinese dumping on the European market or the EU’s dependency on its critical minerals.

stories.title: France records around 1,000 excess deaths in heatwave
stories.summary: French health officials have said there has been around 1,000 more deaths than expected during a record-breaking heatwave that has baked much of western Europe for days. "Since June 24, approximately 1,000 additional deaths (unconsolidated figures) have been observed compared to the deaths recorded in previous months," Public Health France said in a statement. The agency said areas under red alert for heat had been particularly badly affected, and 85% of the deaths had been those aged 65 and over. The sharpest increases, the agency said, involved people dying at home, especially in the Ile-de-France region that includes Paris and its suburbs.

stories.title: What does NATO mean in 2026 under Donald Trump?
stories.summary: Donald Trump is known for his fondness for charts, gold and flattery. NATO's Secretary General Mark Rutte is known for winning over the US president. So, when the so-called 'Trump Whisperer’ is tasked with keeping the president on side ahead of a crucial NATO summer in a fortnight, he rolls into the White House with the receipts and plenty of plámásing. Two large charts, mounted on easels, with gold letters that spelled out ‘Trump Trillions’ accompanied Mr Rutte to the Oval Office on Wednesday.

stories.title: Opposition to development near birthplace of Cú Chulainn
stories.summary: Community campaigners in Dundalk, Co Louth, have voiced their opposition to a proposed housing development close to a historical site which is also said in Irish mythology to be the birthplace of Cú Chulainn. A planning application has been lodged for a large-scale development of 1,058 homes on a 38 hectare site off Mount Avenue and the Castletown Road in Dundalk. The site is close to Dún Dealgan, a national monument in State guardianship. It is also referred to locally as Cú Chulainn's castle. Campaigners have raised concerns about the scale and density of the proposed development and the potential visual impact on the landscape surrounding the monument.
